brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: Level 0 holds three full base cells (-1,0,0), (0,0,0), (1,0,0) plus a half base (0,1,0); level 1 holds three full base cells (-1,0,1), (0,0,1), (1,0,1) stacked over the level-0 row.
Level 1 cells carry bins: bin:-1,0,1 (Bin, full depth), bin:0,0,1 (full depth, 2 compartments), bin:1,0,1 (full depth, 3 compartments).
drawer:0#0,1#cut on the cut face of the half base at (0,1,0) on level 0, under the bin row.
capOpenFaces added 21 solid end caps on every open face; check_build reports no issues and meshClash is clear. lockJoints added 3 joint bolts.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex workbench organizer: a level-0 row of three full bases plus a half base carrying a drawer, and a level-1 row of three full bases carrying three bins of differing compartment layouts. Open faces are capped and joints bolted. check_build is clean with meshClash clear. I did not add props, since the brief did not ask for them. Material suitability for a workbench is not verified by the configurator.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
